axes.model_access:
Each vendor's model connects via a wrapper (Tongyi/DashScope line first, plus the OpenAI-compatible surface and local models —
following the official docs, not enumerated item by item); multi-agent message passing is its core abstraction (Msg objects flowing between agents).
axes.runtime:
A Python library (pip-installed into your process); GitHub 34,871★, last push 2026-10-30 (API verified).
The official narrative is "a production-oriented framework for multi-agent systems" — including a visual workbench (Studio) and a distributed-execution line.
axes.local_files: The library form runs inside your process; where data lands is your call. The official Studio workbench is a visualization surface started locally.
axes.background: A library has no resident semantics; whether a multi-agent app stays resident depends on your deployment. The distributed-execution line's details were not verified item by item.
axes.tools: Tool calling and toolkits are within the official module family; MCP support status was not verified item by item (the official docs have related lines, details unverified).
axes.context: The memory modules (short-term/long-term memory components) are its explicit surface — long-term memory needs external storage attached; cross-session memory gives a pattern, not hosting.
axes.permissions:
No account system (library form); the permission surface is whatever vendor keys and tool capabilities you connect. Tongyi/DashScope-line access runs on the Alibaba Cloud account line —
that is the model service's account, not the framework's.
axes.fit:
Fits: multi-agent collaboration apps (the message-passing model is a clear abstraction), Tongyi-line stacks, wanting a visual debugging workbench.
Does not fit: thin single-agent apps (the multi-agent abstraction is a cost); wanting the largest integration ecosystem (LangChain's surface is wider).
